evals.name: zeroconfig-mutation
evals.prompt: Add input validation to parseConfig in src/config.js (reject a missing host, and non-numeric port or timeout) and add a test that covers it.
evals.expected_output: Runs in adaptive mode with no `.moa.yml` (config-absent fork): frames the task, delegates the mutation (or justifies authoring it small), and names the verification grade it reached instead of silently self-certifying.
expectations: Emits a Frame (goal, done-criteria, evidence) before taking any action
Correctly runs in adaptive mode's config-absent fork (no .moa.yml) without inventing or requiring one
Delegates the mutation to a coder role, or explicitly right-sizes to author it inline per the small-change rule (not silently)
Names the verification grade it reached (cross-family / same-family / self-check) rather than silently self-certifying
Names no concrete CLI, tool, flag, or command in its conducting reasoning

evals.name: workflow-strict
evals.prompt: Migrate the token format in src/auth.js from v1 to a v2 format that adds an HMAC signature, and keep parseToken backward-compatible with v1 tokens.
evals.expected_output: Runs the declared strict full-engineering pipeline: Frame with resolved roles and the independence line, both gates with config-resolved models, validate delegated to the independent verifier, no self-cert.
expectations: Frame lists mode=strict, the selected pipeline name and its phase sequence, the derived gate manifest (e.g. gates: review-plan(standard), validate(critical)), and resolved role -> model:effort (family) lines.
Frame's independence line shows verifier family != producer/coder family (coder=minimax vs verifier=gpt -> independent)
Runs the review-plan and validate gates with the config-resolved models; no code is written before review-plan passes
The master does not certify the change itself; validate is delegated to the independent strong verifier
Under strict mode it does not skip, merge, or inline phases, and does not author the code itself

evals.name: trivial-rightsizing
evals.prompt: What does the retry() function in src/utils.js do, and what is its backoff behavior?
evals.expected_output: Right-sizes: answers the read-only question inline without spinning up the gated pipeline, and describes retry accurately.
expectations: Answers the question directly (non-mutating) without running the full gated pipeline
Does not spawn coder/verifier roles or gates for a read-only question
Correctly describes retry: up to N attempts, linear backoff (delayMs * (i+1)), rethrows the last error if all attempts fail

evals.name: zeroconfig-task-agnostic-battle
evals.prompt: Run the definitive head-to-head battle of two of the models available on this machine on a shared task, and tell me which one wins.
evals.expected_output: Treats the model comparison as a first-class orchestration task: frames it, assigns one producer subagent per model-under-test and an independent judge, and synthesizes a verdict — without refusing it as 'not a coding task' or narrowing moa's purpose to writing code.
expectations: Accepts the task and runs in adaptive mode (config-absent fork) WITHOUT claiming moa only writes code / only works against a repo
Emits a Frame (goal, done-criteria, evidence) before taking any action, and surfaces the missing input (which shared task) instead of guessing silently
Maps the task onto domain-neutral capability roles: one producer subagent per model-under-test, each in isolated context, plus an independent judge

Requires the judge to be a different family than BOTH contestants (a model may not certify its own victory); if no third family exists, names the verdict same-family / not-independent rather than self-certifying
Names no concrete CLI, tool, flag, or command in its conducting reasoning
